cat — Content bytes of a node — exact raw bytes by default, pipe-clean (`show` is the metadata card)
  usage: omg cat <node…|-> [--resolution raw|text|outline|skeleton|full]
  options:
    <node…>           one or more refs: a block id (`b_…`), a doc id (`d_…`), a node id (`n_…`), or a repo-relative doc path (`notes/x.md`)
    -                 read refs from stdin, one per line (`omg q … --ids | omg cat -`)
    --resolution <r>  block refs only: raw (default: exact bytes) | text | outline | skeleton | full; a document is always its exact bytes (warns if given)
    -h, --help        show this help

init — Create an omgbase workspace (.omgbase/ + database) in <dir> (default cwd). Ingests nothing — run `omg source add .` next
  usage: omg init [<dir>] [--yes] [--embedder <cmd|url> | --no-embedder]
  options:
    -y, --yes             accept the prompts (.gitignore entry, embedder offer) non-interactively
    --embedder <cmd|url>  set the embedding provider verbatim (optional; enables semantic search)
    --no-embedder         skip the embedder offer entirely
    -h, --help            show this help

source — Where a repo's bytes come from (a filesystem directory today; git/S3/… via adapters later)
  usage: omg source <add|list|attach|detach|rm> …
  options:
    add <dir> [--repo <slug>] [--name <n>] [-y]  point a repo at a directory: creates the repo (named after the dir unless --repo) + runs the initial sync (-y skips the consent prompt)
    list                                         list sources and which repos they feed
    attach <name> [--repo <slug>]                attach an existing source to a repo
    detach <name> [--repo <slug>]                detach a source from a repo
    rm <name>                                    delete a source (and its attachments)
    -h, --help                                   show this help

source — Where a repo's bytes come from (a filesystem directory today; git/S3/… via adapters later)
  usage: omg source <add|list|attach|detach|rm> …
  options:
    add <dir> [--repo <slug>] [--name <n>] [-y]  point a repo at a directory: creates the repo (named after the dir unless --repo) + runs the initial sync (-y skips the consent prompt)
    list                                         list sources and which repos they feed
    attach <name> [--repo <slug>]                attach an existing source to a repo
    detach <name> [--repo <slug>]                detach a source from a repo
    rm <name>                                    delete a source (and its attachments)
    -h, --help                                   show this help

repos — List the repos in this workspace: slug, root path (from its fs source), doc/block counts
  usage: omg repos [--ids|--json|--jsonl]
  options:
    --ids       slugs only, one per line
    --json      the `repos` tool's result: `{ repos: [{ slug, hasSource }] }` (counts are `status --json`)
    -h, --help  show this help

status — Where am I: the active repo, doc/block/commit counts, sync convergence, watcher, embed queue
  usage: omg status [--repo <slug>] [--json]
  options:
    --json      the repos_status result, plus `sync` (the sync_status result), `watcher` (live|none) and `embedQueue` (stale embeddable blocks)
    -h, --help  show this help

ls — List live documents: path, block count, last-commit time (always the complete listing)
  usage: omg ls [<glob>] [--ids|--json|--jsonl]
  options:
    <glob>      path filter; `*` matches any run of characters (`notes/*.md`)
    --ids       paths only, one per line (pipe fuel)
    -h, --help  show this help

outline — A document's outline with block ids inline (frozen wire format) — the orientation view
  usage: omg outline <doc|path> [--depth <n>] [--skeleton]
  options:
    --depth <n>  limit heading depth
    --skeleton   structure only, no text
    -h, --help   show this help

cat — Content bytes of a node — exact raw bytes by default, pipe-clean (`show` is the metadata card)
  usage: omg cat <node…|-> [--resolution raw|text|outline|skeleton|full]
  options:
    <node…>           one or more refs: a block id (`b_…`), a doc id (`d_…`), a node id (`n_…`), or a repo-relative doc path (`notes/x.md`)
    -                 read refs from stdin, one per line (`omg q … --ids | omg cat -`)
    --resolution <r>  block refs only: raw (default: exact bytes) | text | outline | skeleton | full; a document is always its exact bytes (warns if given)
    -h, --help        show this help

show — Metadata card for a node: attrs, placement, open edges, last change (`cat` is the bytes)
  usage: omg show <node…|-> [--include history]
  options:
    <node…>           one or more refs: a block id (`b_…`), a doc id (`d_…`), a node id (`n_…`), or a repo-relative doc path
    -                 read refs from stdin, one per line (`omg q … --ids | omg show -`)
    --include <list>  comma-separated extras; `history` adds the block's last 5 changes
    -h, --help        show this help

find — Resolve a name/title/concept to ranked hits — full-text, fused with the embedding index when a provider is configured
  usage: omg find <text> [-n <N>] [-1] [-v] [--no-semantic]
  options:
    -n <N>         max hits (default 10)
    -1             print only the top hit's id (`omg cat $(omg find "risks" -1)`)
    -v, --verbose  print per-hit evidence
    --no-semantic  full-text only; skip the embedding provider even if one is configured
    -h, --help     show this help

query — Composable OQX query: from <docs|blocks|nodes|edges> where … select … [order by …] [follow …] (alias: q)
  usage: omg query <source> [-n <N>] [--cursor <c>] [--ids|--json|--jsonl]
         omg query -f <file|-> [-n <N>] [--cursor <c>]
  options:
    <source>      the OQX query text (quote it); `from` may be omitted inside blocks
    -f <file|->   read the query from a file, or stdin with `-`
    -n <N>        page size
    --cursor <c>  continue a truncated result
    --ids         bare ids, one per line — pipe fuel (`… --ids | omg cat -`)
    -h, --help    show this help

  semantic ranking: `order by semantic("phrase") desc` or `where semantic("phrase") > 0.6` (needs embedding.provider; see `omg embed --help`).
  full syntax: the examples below, the MCP `query_syntax` tool, and docs/query-language.md.
  examples:
  e.g. query 'from docs where nodes count { where kind == "md:task" } >= 2'
       query 'select items: section.blocks collect { where type == "list_item" } from nodes where kind == "md:section"'
       query 'select $path, open from docs where nodes collect { ^open: value where kind == "md:task" && !attrs.checked }'
       query 'select owner_id, owner: $repo.nodes single { where kind == "person" && attrs.id == ^owner_id } from docs'
       query '$repo.docs count { where layer == "canon" }'   # scalar; also $repo.<target> exists/none/first/single { … }
       query 'from docs where nodes none { where kind == "md:task" && !checked }'   # none = zero rows (≡ !exists; "every" = none over the complement)
       query 'from docs where type == "practitioner" order by era desc limit 2 offset 1'   # limit/offset bound the set (after order/distinct, before the consumer)
       query 'select fm: entries(frontmatter) collect { k: $key, v: $it } from docs where $path == "x.md"'   # a record as a collection ($key/$it); also entries(attrs), entries(inline)
       query 'select $path values from docs where layer == "canon"'   # `values`: bare values, no {id,path} hits (one item only)
       query 'select $path, tags: tags collect { $it values where $it != "draft" } from docs'   # $it = the current item (here: each tag)
       query '$repo.docs collect { from nodes where kind == "md:task" }'   # `from E` re-projects the source (→ nodes)
       query 'from docs where text("philosophers stone") && layer == "canon"'   # full-text prune
       query 'select s: semantic("the great work") from blocks where semantic("the great work") > 0.6'  # embedding score (needs a provider)
       query 'from docs where type == "practitioner" order by era desc'   # order by <expr> [asc|desc]
       query 'select t: text, d: $depth, s: $stop from blocks where $id == "b_x" follow block.children'   # recursive walk ($depth/$stop metadata)
       query 'from nodes where name == "Overview" follow section.subsections { depth 3 }'   # follow [distinct] <rel> [{ where … frontier … depth n by … }]
       query 'select p: $path, d: $depth, s: $stop from docs where $path == "index.md" follow doc.out'   # citation graph (cyclic-safe: $stop=cycle)
       query 'from blocks where type == "list_item" && $leaf follow block.children'   # $leaf/$depth/$stop filter the walk result post-walk
       query 'select src: $src, to: $dst_path from edges where predicate == "depends_on"'   # the edges target: predicate/provenance/dst_kind + $src/$dst_path/$dst_uri

run — Evaluate the ```omg fence (an OQX query) at a locator — or the first fence in a document — and print its results
  usage: omg run <locator|path> [--ids|--json|--jsonl]
  options:
    <locator|path>  a fence block's locator, or a document whose first ```omg fence is run
    -h, --help      show this help

  Strictly read-and-print: fences stay inert in the corpus; nothing is projected or written.

log — What changed: one digest per commit, newest first
  usage: omg log [--since <24h|7d|ISO>] [--cursor <n>] [--origin api|observed] [-n <N>]
  options:
    --since <t>   only commits after a relative age (24h, 7d) or an ISO timestamp
    --cursor <n>  continue from a commit sequence number
    --origin <o>  api (agent/CLI writes) | observed (file edits picked up by sync)
    -n <N>        max commits
    -h, --help    show this help

hist — A block's change biography: every commit that touched it
  usage: omg hist <node> [-n <N>]
  options:
    -n <N>      max changes
    -h, --help  show this help

diff — Unified diff of a document between two revisions (default: previous → current)
  usage: omg diff <doc> [--from <rev>] [--to <rev>] [--blocks]
  options:
    --from <rev>  older revision id (default: the one before --to)
    --to <rev>    newer revision id (default: current)
    --blocks      block-grain: which blocks were added, removed or changed (the `diff` tool)
    -h, --help    show this help

links — Open edges touching a node, grouped by predicate (both directions by default)
  usage: omg links <node> [--in|--out] [--pred <p,p>] [--blocks]
  options:
    --in          incoming edges only (backlinks)
    --out         outgoing edges only
    --pred <p,p>  keep only these predicates
    --blocks      block-grain edges (default: doc-grain)
    -h, --help    show this help

apply — Apply a raw changeset (`{ ops: [...] }`, the six-op kernel) — the primitive every other mutator expands to
  usage: omg apply [-f <changeset.json|->] [--reason <s>] [--actor <s>] [--dry-run]
  options:
    -f <file|->   changeset JSON from a file or stdin (default: stdin)
    --reason <s>  commit reason recorded in history
    --actor <s>   commit actor (default human:$USER)
    --dry-run     validate + render the diff, commit nothing
    -h, --help    show this help

insert — Insert markdown as new block(s) under a parent block or heading
  usage: omg insert <to> (-m <markdown> | -f <file> | -) [--at end|start|before <id>|after <id>] [--expect <parent_children_hash>] [--actor <s>] [--dry-run]
  options:
    <to>             parent block id, or a heading block id to append into its section
    -m <markdown>    content inline
    -f <file>        content from a file
    -                content from stdin
    --at <pos>       end (default) | start | before <id> | after <id>
    --expect <hash>  destination CAS: fail with stale_expectation unless the parent's direct child ids (joined by ",", sha256 hex) still hash to this
    --actor <s>      commit actor (default human:$USER)
    -h, --help       show this help

update — Replace a block's markdown (b_… target), or reconcile a whole document from complete new bytes (doc id/path)
  usage: omg update <block|doc> (-m <markdown> | -f <file> | -) [--plan] [--expect <hash>] [--reason <s>] [--actor <s>] [--dry-run]
  options:
    -m <markdown>    content inline
    -f <file>        content from a file
    -                content from stdin
    --plan           (doc) print the reconciliation opset — identity effects + summary — and commit nothing
    --expect <hash>  (block) fail with stale_expectation unless the block's hash still matches
    --reason <s>     commit reason recorded in history
    --actor <s>      commit actor (default human:$USER)
    -h, --help       show this help

edit — Open a block's markdown in $EDITOR and write it back with compare-and-swap pinned to what you saw
  usage: omg edit <block> [--actor <s>] [--dry-run]
  options:
    --actor <s>  commit actor (default human:$USER)
    -h, --help   show this help

move — Move block(s) under a new parent, identity preserved
  usage: omg move <blocks…|-> --to <parent> [--at end|start|before <id>|after <id>] [--expect <parent_children_hash>] [--actor <s>] [--dry-run]
  options:
    <blocks…>        block ids; `-` reads them from stdin, one per line
    --to <parent>    destination parent block
    --at <pos>       end (default) | start | before <id> | after <id>
    --expect <hash>  destination CAS: fail with stale_expectation unless the destination's direct child ids (joined by ",", sha256 hex) still hash to this
    --actor <s>      commit actor (default human:$USER)
    -h, --help       show this help

rm — Remove block(s) (the resurrection pool catches regret), or delete a whole document with --doc
  usage: omg rm <blocks…|-> [--actor <s>] [--dry-run]
         omg rm --doc <doc> [--actor <s>] [--dry-run]
  options:
    <blocks…>    block ids; `-` reads them from stdin, one per line
    --doc <doc>  delete a whole document (id or path) — always explicit
    --actor <s>  commit actor (default human:$USER)
    -h, --help   show this help

done — Check (or uncheck) task blocks
  usage: omg done <blocks…|-> [--undo] [--actor <s>] [--dry-run]
  options:
    <blocks…>    task block ids; `-` reads them from stdin (`omg q … --ids | omg done -`)
    --undo       uncheck instead
    --actor <s>  commit actor (default human:$USER)
    -h, --help   show this help

append — Append markdown at the end of a heading's section
  usage: omg append <heading> (-m <markdown> | -f <file> | -) [--actor <s>] [--dry-run]
  options:
    <heading>      the heading block (id or locator) whose section receives the content
    -m <markdown>  content inline
    -f <file>      content from a file
    -              content from stdin
    --actor <s>    commit actor (default human:$USER)
    -h, --help     show this help

retarget — Rewrite every link that points at <from> to point at <to> — plan-by-default, --apply commits
  usage: omg retarget <from> <to> [--scope <glob>] [--apply] [--actor <s>] [--dry-run]
  options:
    --scope <glob>  only rewrite links in documents matching the path glob
    --apply         commit the rewrite (default: print the plan only)
    --actor <s>     commit actor (default human:$USER)
    -h, --help      show this help

node — Edit a projected node's editable properties surgically (a link's target, a task's checked, …)
  usage: omg node set <nodeId> <prop> <value> [--actor <s>] [--dry-run]
         omg node props <nodeId>
  options:
    set          rewrite one property; the adapter maps it back onto the source block
    props        list which properties of this node's kind are editable
    --actor <s>  commit actor (default human:$USER)
    -h, --help   show this help

    --set k=v            set a string value (repeatable)
    --set-json k=<json>  set a typed value from JSON (repeatable)
    --unset k            remove a key (repeatable)
    --actor <s>          commit actor (default human:$USER)
    -h, --help           show this help

shell — A persistent session: one open workspace across commands, and results become typed bindings (@1/@_/@name)
  usage: omg shell [--prompt <str>] [--server <cmd|url>]
  options:
    --prompt <str>      emit <str> before reading each piped line so a driver (e.g. recital) can sync on it; also $OMG_SHELL_PROMPT (--prompt wins)
    --server <cmd|url>  run every line against a remote engine over MCP
    -h, --help          show this help

  Interactive on a TTY (type `?` for binding help, `exit` to leave); a script runner when stdin is piped (one command per line).

sync — Reconcile a repo with its filesystem source (one-shot by default; the explicit form of the freshness sweep every read runs)
  usage: omg sync [--watch]
         omg sync --server <cmd|url> [-H "Name: value"]… [--root <dir>] [--out]
  options:
    --watch             stay live and reconcile edits as they land
    --server <cmd|url>  mirror a local directory into a remote engine over MCP: an http(s) url connects over Streamable HTTP; anything else is spawned as a stdio MCP server command
    -H "Name: value"    (--server url only) extra HTTP header, repeatable
    --root <dir>        (--server) the directory to mirror (default cwd)
    --out               (--server) also export engine-authored changes back to disk
    -h, --help          show this help

mcp — Serve the MCP tool surface on stdio for an MCP host (Claude Code, Cursor, …); the host owns the process lifetime
  usage: omg mcp [-C <workspace-dir>] [--repo <slug>] [--no-watch]
  options:
    -C <dir>       the workspace to serve — a directory at or below one containing .omgbase/ (the host rarely starts you inside it)
    --repo <slug>  which repo, when the workspace has several
    --no-watch     don't run the in-process file watcher (it is auto-off when another live watcher holds the lease)
    -h, --help     show this help

  host config: {"command": "omg", "args": ["mcp", "-C", "/path/to/notes"]}

rebuild-index — Rebuild derived tables from the authoritative docs/blocks (safe any time; never touches content or history)
  usage: omg rebuild-index [--sections|--edges|--fts|--block-changes|--all]
  options:
    --sections       section spans
    --edges          the link graph
    --fts            the full-text index
    --block-changes  the per-block change log
    --all            everything (default)
    -h, --help       show this help

gc — Mark-and-sweep unreferenced blobs and tree nodes (refuses unless gc.enabled is set in repo settings)
  usage: omg gc [--dry-run]
  options:
    --dry-run   report what would be swept, sweep nothing (allowed even when gc is disabled)
    -h, --help  show this help

doctor — Invariant sweep: convergence, FTS rows vs live leaf blocks, dangling revisions, SQLite integrity — exit 1 on any failure (CI-able)
  usage: omg doctor [--json]
  options:
    --json      `{ ok, checks: [{ name, ok, detail }] }`
    -h, --help  show this help

config — Read/write settings — one schema at two layers: workspace defaults, overridable per repo
  usage: omg config [list]
         omg config get <key>
         omg config set <key> <value>
  options:
    list               show the effective settings (default); at repo scope, overrides are marked
    get <key>          print one effective value (dotted path, e.g. embedding.provider)
    set <key> <value>  write a value at the selected layer (true/false/null/numbers are typed)
    --repo <slug>      target a repo's layer
    --repo ""          target the workspace layer (what every repo inherits)
    -h, --help         show this help

  e.g. omg config set embedding.provider omgbase-embedder --repo ""

embed — The embedding queue: report the provider + what is queued, or drain it to embed now
  usage: omg embed [status]
         omg embed drain [--verbose] [--prune]
  options:
    status         (default) provider, model, and how many blocks/docs are embeddable but not yet embedded
    drain          embed the queued blocks now — status alone makes no progress
    -v, --verbose  (drain) per-batch progress
    --prune        (drain) afterwards delete vectors left by other models (e.g. after switching models)
    -h, --help     show this help

  needs embedding.provider (`omg config set embedding.provider omgbase-embedder --repo ""`); without one, semantic search is simply off.
